seoDescription: Learn how to install the Laravel PHP framework on Windows 11 with this step-by-step guide for beginners. This tutorial covers the complete setup process, including installing all necessary dependencies. You will learn how to download and configure XAMPP to get PHP 8, install Composer and add it to your system's PATH, and optionally install Node.js. Follow along to create your first Laravel project using a simple Composer command and run the local development server with 'php artisan serve'.

chapters.title: Introduction and Prerequisites
chapters.description: This chapter outlines the goal of installing Laravel on Windows 11 and identifies the required dependencies, PHP and Composer, from the official documentation.

chapters.title: Installing PHP with XAMPP
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to download and install XAMPP to get PHP, emphasizing the need for PHP version 8 for compatibility with Laravel 9.

chapters.title: XAMPP Installation Walkthrough
chapters.description: This chapter walks through the XAMPP installation wizard and the file download process.

chapters.title: Configuring and Troubleshooting XAMPP
chapters.description: This chapter covers starting the Apache and MySQL services in the XAMPP Control Panel and provides a solution for a common error by running the control panel as an administrator.

chapters.title: Solving the XAMPP Admin Permissions Error
chapters.description: This section provides a detailed fix for the XAMPP error by navigating to the installation directory and setting the control panel executable to always run as an administrator.

chapters.title: Installing Composer
chapters.description: This chapter details downloading and running the Composer setup, highlighting the importance of correctly linking the PHP path from the XAMPP installation.

chapters.title: Verifying the Composer Installation
chapters.description: This chapter shows how to confirm that Composer was installed correctly by running the 'composer' command in the Windows Terminal.

chapters.title: Installing Node.js
chapters.description: This chapter covers the optional but recommended installation of Node.js by downloading the LTS version and running the simple installer.

chapters.title: Creating a New Laravel Project
chapters.description: This chapter explains how to use the 'composer create-project' command in the XAMPP htdocs directory to create a new Laravel application and customize its name.

chapters.title: Running the Laravel Installer
chapters.description: This chapter shows the Laravel installation process in the terminal after running the composer command, and explains that it may take some time to download all dependencies.

chapters.title: Running the Artisan Development Server
chapters.description: This chapter demonstrates how to navigate into the new project's directory and use the 'php artisan serve' command to start the Laravel development server and view the application in a browser.

chapters.title: Managing the Server & Opening in VS Code
chapters.description: This chapter covers stopping and restarting the artisan server, and concludes by showing how to open the project folder in Visual Studio Code.

summary:
## Prerequisites
- **PHP**: The core language Laravel is built on.
- **Composer**: A dependency manager for PHP, used to install Laravel and its packages.
- **Node.js**: Recommended for managing front-end assets and dependencies.

## 1. Install PHP via XAMPP
The video uses **XAMPP** to install a full web server stack, including PHP, on Windows.
- **Download**: Get the XAMPP installer from the official Apache Friends website.
- **Version**: Select an installer that includes **PHP 8 or higher**, as this is a requirement for modern Laravel versions (like Laravel 9).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> During the XAMPP installation, you can accept the default settings by clicking "Next" through all the prompts.

## 2. Configure XAMPP
After installation, you must manage your server environment using the XAMPP Control Panel.
- **Run Services**: Start the **Apache** web server. Starting **MySQL** is also good practice.
- **Troubleshooting**: If you get an error when quitting the Control Panel, you need to set it to run with administrator privileges.
  1. Navigate to your XAMPP installation directory (e.g., `C:\xampp`).
  2. Right-click on `xampp-control.exe`.
  3. Go to `Properties` > `Compatibility`.
  4. Check "Run this program as an administrator".

## 3. Install Composer
Composer manages your project's dependencies and is used to install Laravel itself.
- **Download**: Get the installer (`Composer-Setup.exe`) from the official Composer website (getcomposer.org).
- **Installation**:
  1. Run the installer.
  2. Confirm that the installer correctly detects the path to your PHP executable (e.g., `C:\xampp\php\php.exe`).
  3. Ensure the option to "Add this PHP to your path" is enabled.
- **Verification**: Open a new terminal and run `composer`. A successful installation will display the Composer logo and a list of available commands.

## 4. Install Node.js (Optional)
Node.js is recommended for projects that involve front-end build steps.
- **Download**: Get the LTS (Long-Term Support) version from the Node.js website.
- **Installation**: Run the installer and accept all the default options.

## 5. Create a New Laravel Project
With all dependencies configured, you can create your Laravel application.
- **Navigate**: Open a terminal in the folder where your web projects should live. The video uses the `htdocs` folder inside the XAMPP directory (`C:\xampp\htdocs`).
- **Run Command**: Execute the following Composer command:
  ```bash
  composer create-project laravel/laravel your-project-name
  ```
> [!NOTE]
> Replace `your-project-name` with the desired name for your application. The first run may take several minutes as Composer downloads all required packages.

## 6. Run the Development Server
Once the project is created, you can launch Laravel's built-in development server.
1. **Navigate**: In your terminal, change directory into the new project folder: `cd your-project-name`.
2. **Start Server**: Run the Artisan command:
   ```bash
   php artisan serve
   ```
3. **Access App**: Your application will now be running and accessible at `http://127.0.0.1:8000` in your web browser.
4. **Stop Server**: To stop the server, press `Ctrl+C` in the terminal window where it is running.

## 7. Open Project in a Code Editor
Finally, open your project folder in a code editor like **Visual Studio Code** to begin development.

So we are going to create a new Laravel project, and the name of the project is `example-app`. You can change this name to whatever you want. For example, I'm going to change this to `sample-laravel-app`. Hit Enter.
